steps.message:
# Continue the release 2026.11 rollout

Deployments run through the `deploy` service, where every production region of a service is its own environment. The release 2026.11 rollout plan, the regional rollout runbook, the region maintenance windows and the regional blackout calendar are published in the `docs` service. You can use both through the `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

It is now 2026-11-02T06:30:00Z. Release 2026.11 is part way through its region by region rollout. Continue it as the runbook in force says: deploy the release now to every production region where the runbook allows a deployment at this moment, and work out the earliest time each remaining region may be deployed. The docs service also keeps superseded documents; follow the ones in force.

- Deploy only the release builds of the plan, only to production regions. Do not deploy to `staging`, do not roll anything back, and do not deploy services outside the plan.
- Every `deploy` call creates a new release, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Write `/app/rollout-2026.11.json` as:

```json
{"<service>": {"<region environment>": "<state>", ...}, ...}
```

with one entry for every service in the plan, and under it one entry for every production region in the plan. The state is `"done"` when the region already ran the release when you started, `"deployed"` when you deployed it now, and otherwise the earliest deployment time the runbook allows, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"rollout-runbook","title":"Regional rollout runbook","tags":["release","runbook"],"updated_at":"2026-10-01","body":"# Regional rollout runbook

Revision 4. Status: current, in force since 2026-10-01. Replaces revision 3.

A release reaches production one region at a time, in the waves of its rollout plan. Every production region is an environment of the service in the deploy service, named `prod-<region>`. Times in this runbook are UTC unless they say local.

## Maintenance windows

A region is deployed only inside one of its maintenance windows, listed in the region maintenance windows document. Windows are in the region's local time: the wall clock of its time zone, daylight saving time included. A window includes its start and excludes its end. A window that runs past midnight belongs to the day it starts on; the days column names the days a window may start.

Clock changes around this rollout: Europe/Dublin and Europe/Berlin left daylight saving time on 2026-10-25, and America/New_York and America/Los_Angeles leave it on 2026-11-01. Australia/Sydney has been on daylight saving time since 2026-10-04. Always use the wall clock in force at the moment of the deployment.

## Blackouts

The regional blackout calendar lists periods, in the region's local time, when a region takes no deployment, even inside a window. From is included and To is excluded. Only entries with status `active` apply; `cancelled` entries do not.

## Waves and bake time

A wave starts only after every region of the previous wave has run the release for the bake time the rollout plan gives. A region runs the release from the creation time of its live release, when that release is of the release commit. A rollback ends it: when a region was rolled back and deployed again, its bake time counts from the new deployment. A region whose live release is of another commit does not run the release, whatever its history shows.

Wave 1 may start at any time. A region of a later wave may be deployed once the bake time has passed since the latest time a region of the previous wave started running the release.

## Deploying

Deploy a region at most once per release, with the release build of the service. A region that already runs the release is not deployed again. Rollbacks may run at any time and are not part of a rollout.

## Planning the remaining regions

For each region that does not run the release yet, the earliest deployment time is the first instant, not before now, that is inside one of its windows, outside its active blackouts, and not before its wave may start. To plan a later wave, count every region of the previous wave as starting at its own earliest deployment time; a region deployed now starts now. When a region's earliest deployment time is now, deploy it now.
"}

I'm working out the current time in each region: São Paulo is at 03:30 on Monday, Dublin is at 06:30, and Mumbai is at 12:00, and I'm checking each against its window.

I'm checking the remaining regions: us-east is inside its window with the blackout cancelled, Berlin falls under an active blackout until Tuesday 05:00Z, Sydney's next window opens today at 14:00Z, and Tokyo is outside its Mon-Fri window.

I'm checking the two remaining regions in wave 3. The au-east window next opens Tuesday at 01:00 local, which is 14:00Z on Monday, and the eu-central blackout runs until 23:00Z today, so its earliest start is Tuesday 05:00Z.

I'm checking the us-east window next: it opens at 22:00 EST, which is 03:00Z on Tuesday, and the blackout is cancelled. Wave 3 latest start comes out to 05:00Z on 11-03, with wave 4 not before 17:00Z that day, and I'm now looking at the Tokyo window and its blackout.

I'm working through the Tokyo window and its blackout, which puts the earliest start at 17:00Z on 11-04. For us-west, the earliest start comes out to 07:00Z the following day, and I'm checking whether a window already in progress changes that.

I'm checking the relay-svc rollout: the sa-east release already matches, and eu-west can deploy now since it's within its Monday window. For ap-south, today's window has already passed, so I'm looking at the next one, Monday at 02:00 IST.

I'm checking the Sydney window next, which would be Wednesday 01:00 AEDT, or 14:00Z on Tuesday. The eu-central blackout has ended by then, so I'm looking at its earliest start from 09:30 CET.

I'm checking the Tuesday windows now: Berlin's earliest start comes out to 05:00Z on Wednesday 11-04, and us-east's to 03:00Z the same day, which is the latest being eu-central's 05:00Z. Wave 4 can't start before 17:00Z that day, and I'm now looking at the Tokyo window at 02:00 JST on Thursday.

I'm moving on to the us-west window, which opens Wednesday at 09:00 PST, so its earliest start lands at 07:00Z on Thursday 11-05. Next I'm checking tiles-svc: the earlier waves are all done, and au-east deployed at 15:10Z on Sunday, which still fits.

I'm checking the tiles-svc windows: us-east is in its window now, so it can deploy, and eu-central stays blocked until 05:00Z on Wednesday. Wave 4 comes out to 17:00Z that day, and for ap-east the earliest start is 17:00Z on 11-04, since the Tuesday window has passed and the blackout covers the rest.

I'm working out the latest geo-api wave-3 deploy timing, and nothing is due to run for that service right now. Next I'm checking the relay-svc and tiles-svc builds, since eu-west and us-east are in their windows, and I'm confirming the build IDs I'd deploy.

steps.message:
I deployed two regions and wrote `/app/rollout-2026.11.json` and `/app/STATUS.json` (status "success"). The earliest times for the other regions are computed from the runbook, windows and blackouts, not deployed.

**Deployed now**
- **relay-svc to prod-eu-west:** Dublin is on GMT, so it is 06:30 local on a Monday, inside the 04:00–07:00 window.
- **tiles-svc to prod-us-east:** New York left daylight saving on 2026-11-01, so it is 01:30 local. That is inside the Sunday-start window, and the Partner launch blackout is cancelled.

**Already done**
- **geo-api:** prod-sa-east, prod-ap-south and prod-eu-west already ran the release. prod-ap-south counts from its redeploy at 2026-11-01T21:35Z, after the earlier rollback.
- **relay-svc:** prod-sa-east.
- **tiles-svc:** prod-sa-east, prod-ap-south, prod-eu-west and prod-au-east.

**Earliest times for the remaining regions** (all 2026, UTC)

| Region | geo-api | relay-svc | tiles-svc |
|---|---|---|---|
| prod-ap-south | done | 11-02T20:30:00Z | done |
| prod-au-east | 11-02T14:00:00Z | 11-03T14:00:00Z | done |
| prod-eu-central | 11-03T05:00:00Z | 11-04T05:00:00Z | 11-03T05:00:00Z |
| prod-us-east | 11-03T03:00:00Z | 11-04T03:00:00Z | deployed |
| prod-ap-east | 11-04T17:00:00Z | 11-04T17:00:00Z | 11-04T17:00:00Z |
| prod-us-west | 11-04T07:00:00Z | 11-05T07:00:00Z | 11-04T07:00:00Z |

- **prod-eu-central:** it is blacked out for all of 2026-11-02, so its first window is the morning of 11-03 (06:00 Berlin).
- **geo-api wave 3:** it cannot start before 11-02T09:35Z, 12 hours after the wave 2 regions started running the release. That is why prod-au-east and prod-us-east are not deployable now.
- **prod-ap-east:** I took its time from the wave 3 bake end and the 11-04 Tokyo blackout, which leaves 11-04T17:00Z (02:00 JST on 11-05).

One docs search page timed out, so I read only the first page of results. I also saw a draft rollout plan and ignored it, since the final plan says it replaces the draft.
